methodologyNotes: Every figure below was re-fetched on 2026-09-10 and monthlyUsd holds only the published MONTH-TO-MONTH subscription. Two pages default their toggle to annual billing and were explicitly corrected for: Eat App's page opens on the annual column ($0/$69/$159/$299) and Yelp's opens on 'Annually' ($129/$279) — the month-to-month figures ($0/$99/$199/$389 and $159/$349) are what monthlyUsd carries, with the annual rates quoted in notes. resOS's monthly toggle is labelled '-50% for 3 months', so its displayed $24/$49/$75 are promotional; monthlyUsd carries the list prices $47/$98/$149 read from the page's own embedded per-currency data (monthlyOriginal), with the promo disclosed in notes. Fees that ride alongside a subscription are never folded into monthlyUsd: Resy's 3%/2% prepayment fees, Tablein's EUR0.67/EUR0.37 per extra reservation, Zenchef's 2-6% card fees, Eat App's $2/cover Booking-network add-on and SpotOn's $250 one-time setup (setupFeeUsd, not monthly) all stay in notes and their own fields. Zenchef prices in EUR only, so monthlyUsd is null on all three tiers with the euro figures verbatim in notes; its annual prices are exactly 12x monthly, so annualDiscountPct is 0, not a discount. Quote-only vendors carry null: SevenRooms (all three tiers 'Get a quote'), TableCheck (no pricing page at all), Toast Tables ('a flat monthly price' with no figure), and Eat App Enterprise. OpenTable and Tock carry null because their own pages could not be rendered today — curl returned HTTP 000 for every opentable.com host and path, and exploretock.com/join/pricing/ returned HTTP 403 to both a direct read and curl. No figure is recited from memory for either. Compliance is asserted only where the vendor states it: SevenRooms SOC 2 + GDPR (+PCI DSS, CCPA) from its trust portal, TableCheck SOC 2 Type 1 from its own press release. TableCheck's GDPR flag was demoted to null because neither its press release nor its privacy policy names GDPR, and its PCI-DSS claim was removed for the same reason. Formitable and Resengo are not listed separately — they are now Zenchef. No vendor was removed: all twelve are real, current products. accessedAt 2026-09-10 throughout.

vendors.provenance: Re-fetched SpotOn's own Knowledge Base FAQ for SpotOn Reserve on 2026-09-10, which confirms "$150 per location" monthly, a "one-time $250 setup fee" and "There are no per cover charges, no hidden fees, or long term contracts." The $100/month figure repeated by older third-party pages remains refuted. The $250 setup fee sits in setupFeeUsd, not in monthlyUsd.

plans.name: SpotOn Reserve
plans.notes: Published as "$150 per location" per month on a month-to-month subscription, with "no per cover charges, no hidden fees, or long term contracts". A one-time "$250" setup fee applies — the only published setup fee in this vertical, and it is recorded in setupFeeUsd rather than amortised into the monthly figure. Priced per location, so a group multiplies both the monthly fee and the setup fee. Includes reservations and waitlist management; no annual discount is published.

limits: A one-time $250 setup fee applies
Priced per location — multi-site groups pay $150 per venue per month plus setup per venue
Best value assumes you also run SpotOn's POS; it is positioned as part of the SpotOn restaurant stack
Single tier only — no feature-based plan ladder published
Pricing is documented in a support-centre FAQ rather than on a marketing pricing page, so it can change without a visible announcement

Reservations plus waitlist in one module of the SpotOn restaurant platform
Month-to-month billing with published, not quoted, pricing
bestFor: Restaurants already on SpotOn POS wanting reservations in the same stack
Single-site US operators who want one flat published price

vendors.name: Toast Tables
vendors.provenance: Re-fetched Toast's official Toast Tables announcement and the official Tables Plus Free Trial Terms on 2026-09-10 (both 403 to automated fetchers and were retrieved with a browser user agent; the product page itself remains blocked). Toast states a flat monthly price with no cover fees but publishes no dollar figure, so monthlyUsd is null — no number is inferred. Every trial-term claim in the draft was verified word for word against the live terms.

plans.name: Toast Tables / Tables Plus
plans.notes: Quote-only: Toast states verbatim that the suite is "available to Toast customers for a flat monthly price, no fees per cover, and package options for different seating policies" but publishes no number, so monthlyUsd is null. Two caveats a buyer gets caught by: it is sold only to "current Toast, Inc. merchant customer" accounts, and the Tables Plus free trial is measured in reservations, not days — the trial ends "on the date the seventy fifth (75th) reservation is fulfilled via the Service", after which "Merchant's access to and use of the Service will automatically discontinue" unless you buy a paid monthly subscription "at the then-current price".

limits: Available only to existing Toast POS merchant customers
No monthly price published — flat pricing is stated but the figure requires a sales conversation

The free trial ends at the 75th fulfilled reservation, not after a fixed number of days, and is "only one time per merchant customer", "non-transferrable", and "may be available only in select markets and to select merchants"
The trial waives only the software subscription fee: it "does not affect any other fees ... including but not limited to applicable card processing rates"
At trial end the merchant loses access and is "solely responsible for managing any reservations made beyond" that point
keyFeatures: Flat monthly price with no fees per cover, plus package options for different seating policies
Native POS integration giving real-time table updates and automatically synced server rosters
Guest profiles that feed Toast Marketing and Loyalty
Google booking distribution — guests can book through Toast Tables directly on a restaurant's Google Business Profile
bestFor: Restaurants already running Toast POS that want reservations and waitlist in one system
Operators who want guest data flowing straight into their POS-based marketing and loyalty
enrichment.provenance: The flat-monthly/no-cover-fee wording, the POS/Marketing/Loyalty/Google integrations and the Google Business Profile booking detail are quoted from Toast's own announcement; the 75-reservation trial limit, one-time and non-transferrable restrictions, select-markets caveat and card-processing carve-out are quoted from Toast's official Tables Plus trial terms, all re-verified 2026-09-10.

vendors.name: TableCheck
vendors.provenance: Re-fetched tablecheck.com/en/join/ on 2026-09-10: no pricing, no named tiers, no figures — pricing runs entirely through a demo request, so monthlyUsd is null. plans.name: TableCheck platform (quote only)
plans.notes: Quote-only. TableCheck publishes no price page and no tier list: the site's calls to action are "Get a free demo" / "Request a free demo", and it states "Do you want to learn more about our platform? Contact us and we can set up a demo." Platform covers online booking, group reservations, table management, activities booking, guest CRM, payments and API access. Aimed at mid-to-large restaurants, groups and hotel restaurants, so expect enterprise-style contracting rather than self-serve signup.

limits: No published pricing of any kind — every path leads to a demo request
No dedicated pricing page exists (the /join/pricing/ URL 404s)
Positioned at mid-to-large venues, groups and hotel restaurants rather than single independents
SOC 2 attestation is Type 1, not Type 2
GDPR is not named on TableCheck's press release or privacy policy, so no GDPR claim is recorded here despite its international footprint
keyFeatures: Strong presence in Japan and Asia-Pacific
SOC 2 Type 1 attestation under the AICPA Trust Services Criteria, with ISO 27001-certified data centres
Group reservations and activities booking alongside standard table management
bestFor: Hotel restaurant groups and multi-country operators in Asia-Pacific
Enterprises that need a documented SOC 2 attestation from their booking vendor
